_comment: EBBMERE - the tidal flats. A walk-and-wonder world: wet sand that holds the sky, tide pools, creeks, shell ridges and a lighthouse. The TIDE goes out and comes back on a shared clock (tide: a pure function of UTC time, TideClock / Server.Tide); tide.field is the baked seabed (one 16-bit value per 16 px cell) the water covers whenever the level is above it; elevation under tide.deep_elev is open sea, walled with invisible 'eb_shore' posts. Eight regions: Dune Landing (where you arrive), Wrack Line, Cockle Ridge, Pool Terrace, The Creeks, Far Bars, Lantern Point and Greywater. It RE-SKINS ITSELF through its 'art' block: its own sand + shore-litter atlas, windswept dune trees, a lighthouse landmark. 'dig' holds the buried spots; its secret is a sand-dollar that only the lowest tide gives up: see the 'secret' block (reveal type 'tide'). Generated by tools/gen_ebbmere_world.py (art: pokepals/tools/gen_ebbmere.py) - edit that and re-run, don't hand-tune positions.
intro: The sea has gone out and left its floor lying about. Walk on it while it lasts.

hints.ebbing: The tide is going out. The flats are opening up, a little further every minute.
hints.low_soon: The water is drawing right back from the far bars. Lowest tide is close.
hints.low: Lowest tide. The far bars are bare, and whatever the sea keeps there is within reach. Be quick: it will not stay.
hints.low_short: Lowest tide. The far bars are bare.
hints.flooding: The tide has turned. The sea is coming back, slowly, over the sand.
hints.high: High water. Everything on the flats is under a hand's depth of sea. Wait for it to go out again.

lines.sniff: Your companion stops, nose to the sand. Something is buried there.
lines.sign: A little ring of bubbles in the wet sand: something is under there. Tap it to send your companion to dig.
lines.cant_dig: Your companion pats at the sand, but this shape cannot dig. A fox, a rabbit or a wolf could.
lines.dug: Already dug. The sea will have the hole filled in by the next tide.
lines.dig_shell: Your companion digs up a %s and drops it at your feet.
lines.dig_crab: A crab! It had been asleep under there, and is now very much awake. It scuttles for the sea.
lines.dig_glass: A piece of sea-glass, worn soft as a sweet. Your companion looks very pleased with itself.
lines.dig_dollar: Under the sand, pale and perfectly round: a sand-dollar, with a flower pressed into its back.

props.label: a stone with waves cut in it
props.lore: Wavy lines are cut into the face of the stone, row on row, and under them a few words in a careful hand: 'It goes out, it comes back. Go down to the flats while the water is away. Your companion has a nose for what it leaves behind. Lowest of all, the far bars show, and what is under them rises.'

props.label: a little cairn
props.lore: Three stones, stacked above the high-water line by someone who trusted the tide to leave them alone. It has.

props.label: a stranded rowboat
props.lore: A rowboat, left on its keel on the ridge by a tide that never came back for it. The paint has gone to chalk. In the bottom, a good many shells, collected by something that was not you.

props.label: a red buoy
props.lore: A buoy, left high and dry. Whoever it was marking is long gone, but the far bars are out this way. They are only bare at the very lowest water.

props.label: an old groyne post
props.lore: One of a row of posts that once held the sand in place. The sand left anyway, and came back, and left.

props.label: an old groyne post
props.lore: Barnacles all the way up to where the highest tide reaches, and none above it.

props.label: an old groyne post
props.lore: The third post, a little shorter, as if the sea had been nibbling at it for years. It has.

props.label: a barnacled rock
props.lore: The rock the lighthouse stands on, here at the point's foot. Under the barnacles, a smooth patch where hands have rested.

props.label: a cairn on the point
props.lore: Built by lamplighters, one stone a night. Nobody ever knocks it down. Nobody ever finishes it either.

props.label: a bleached log
props.lore: A log from somewhere much further away than this. You wonder what it saw. It would say 'water', mostly.

props.label: a heap of shells
props.lore: Cockles, whelks and razor shells, heaped by wind and waves along the ridge. A scallop on top is the pink of the inside of a lip.

props.label: a heap of wrack
props.lore: Seaweed, left in a line where the last tide turned. It smells exactly like the word 'sea'.

_secret_comment: This world's one SECRET (docs/home-world-and-secrets-design.md, 'Ebbmere'). reveal.type 'tide': at the lowest tide the far bar at 'position' is bare; a companion in a form that can dig (dig.affordances) sent to the dig spot 'bar_dollar' brings up the sand-dollar, but only while the shared tide (TideClock; the same clock Server.Tide checks) is in its low window. The server honours the claim only inside that window plus 'grace_s', within 'radius' of 'position'.

secret.lore: A sand-dollar, whole and unbroken, pale as the moon, with a five-petalled flower pressed into its back by a sea that was fond of it. It is the weight of nothing at all.

reveal.reveal_line: Under the sand, pale and perfectly round: a sand-dollar, with a flower pressed into its back.
reveal.refused_line: The tide has turned, and the sea has slipped back over the bar. The sand-dollar is still there. It will rise again at the next lowest tide.

secret.found_line: The sand-dollar was only ever under the lowest water. You and your companion found the one hour of the tide that lets it be seen.

keepsake.label: a sand-dollar in a dish of sand
keepsake.line: A sand-dollar in a shallow dish of sand. If you hold your ear to it, there is nothing at all, and the nothing is the sea.

portals.label: the way back to the Vale
